events.title: House Republicans propose fees on asylum seekers, unaccompanied minors, and humanitarian parole applicants
events.summary: House Republicans, led by Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan, introduced legislation as part of a broader spending and taxation package that would establish new fees on immigrants seeking asylum ($1,000), humanitarian parole ($1,000), work permits ($550), and custody of unaccompanied minors ($3,500–$5,000). events.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump administration's emergency appeal to resume Alien Enemies Act deportations of Venezuelans
events.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's emergency appeal to lift a temporary block on deportations of Venezuelans under the Alien Enemies Act of 1798. Over two dissenting votes (Alito and Thomas), the Court returned the case to federal appeals court and upheld a halt on deportations from a north Texas detention facility. The decision emphasized that detainees must be given reasonable time and notice to contest removal, rejecting the administration's proposed 12-hour window. The ruling cited the wrongful deportation of Kilmar Ábrego García to El Salvador as evidence of systemic risk.
events.why_relevant: The Court's decision constrains executive power to use wartime law for mass deportations without due process, protecting constitutional protections and the rule of law against unilateral executive action.
events.basis: The supreme court has rejected the Trump administration's request to remove a temporary block on deportations of Venezuelans under a rarely used 18th-century wartime law.

events.title: Former California deputy repays stolen cash; felony charges dismissed, peace officer certification surrendered
events.summary: John Sanzone, a former Glenn County sheriff's deputy, stole $3,500 from a homeless man he arrested in 2023. Sanzone attempted to cover up the theft by driving the victim to another county. In May 2023, Sanzone was arrested and charged with grand theft by embezzlement. events.title: President Truman convened President's Committee on Civil Rights
events.summary: After learning from NAACP leader Walter Francis White about World War II veteran Isaac Woodard, who was blinded by a police officer and deputy in South Carolina, President Harry S. events.summary: Since Senate Bill 1 (SB 1) took effect in 2022, mail-in ballot rejection rates in Latino-majority Texas counties surged dramatically. events.federal_nexus: The disparate impact on Latino voters raises potential Voting Rights Act Section 2 claims and equal protection concerns under the Fourteenth Amendment.

events.title: SCOTUS affirms judgment in Baker v. Coates due to lack of quorum
events.summary: In case 24-6839 (Baker v. Coates, Ta-Nehisi, et al.), the Supreme Court lacked a quorum and the qualified Justices determined the case could not be heard and decided at the next Term. Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 2109, the Court entered an order affirming the judgment of the lower court with the same effect as an affirmance by an equally divided court. Justices Alito, Sotomayor, Gorsuch, Barrett, and Jackson took no part in the consideration or decision.
events.why_relevant: Affirmance by operation of law due to lack of quorum is a rare procedural outcome that leaves the lower-court judgment intact without full Court review, affecting the parties and potentially signaling institutional constraints.
events.basis: Because the Court lacks a quorum, 28 U. S. C. §1, and since the qualified Justices are of the opinion that the case cannot be heard and determined at the next Term of the Court, the judgment is affirmed under 28 U. S. C. §2109.

events.title: Oregon counties misallocate addiction-treatment grants to law enforcement instead of services
events.summary: Oregon distributed $20m in state grants to counties for "deflection" programs intended to connect people with substance-use disorders to treatment rather than arrest. Budget documents reveal multiple counties spent the majority of funds on prosecutor salaries, sheriff positions, police vehicles, and drug-detection devices (TruNarc spectrometers) rather than treatment services. Washington County allocated nearly $700,000 of its $1.5m budget to law enforcement positions while only $360,000 went to peer mentors. Despite nearly 7,000 possession arrests statewide since September, only 723 people enrolled in deflection and 88 completed the program. Treatment providers report budget cuts and long waitlists.
events.why_relevant: Misallocation of public health funds toward criminalization rather than treatment undermines the stated policy goal of treating addiction as a public health crisis and perpetuates punitive approaches that have failed for decades, eroding public trust in government resource stewardship.
events.basis: Budget documents obtained by the Guardian through public records requests reveal that several counties have put the money toward hiring prosecutors, acquiring police gadgets and police vehicles, and covering sheriff costs.

events.title: US Supreme Court restores Maine lawmaker's voting rights after legislative censure

events.summary: Following an emergency hearing, Judge Murphy found the government violated the court's preliminary injunction by deporting at least six members of the class to South Sudan without meaningful opportunity to assert claims of protection under the Torture Convention. Judge Murphy held that “no reasonable interpretation of the Court's Preliminary Injunction” could endorse the government's action. The court issued a “summary and clarification” of the injunction requiring removal to a third country to include written notice to both the non-citizen and the non-citizen's counsel in a language the non-citizen can understand, and a meaningful opportunity and a minimum of ten days to raise a fear-based claim for Torture Convention protection (plus an additional 15 days if to seek reopening of immigration proceedings if initially denied). Also following the emergency hearing, Judge Murphy issued a separate order to remedy the violation of the preliminary injunction. It requires giving the six individuals a reasonable fear of torture interview including access to counsel, an interpreter, and technology for transfer of documents “commensurate with the access that they would have received had these procedures occurred within the United States prior to their deportation.”

events.title: Missouri legislature passes deceptively worded referendum to repeal abortion rights amendment
events.summary: On May 21, 2025, the Missouri legislature passed House Joint Resolution 73, a referendum that would amend the state constitution to ban nearly all abortions (with narrow exceptions for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, rape, and incest up to 12 weeks) and ban youth gender-affirming care. The referendum's ballot summary deliberately omits that it would repeal the voter-approved Amendment 3 (which established abortion rights until fetal viability) and instead uses language suggesting it would "allow abortions" and "ensure women's safety"—a material misrepresentation of the measure's actual effect. Governor Kehoe will decide whether to place it on the 2026 ballot or call a special election.
events.why_relevant: The legislature's passage of a referendum with deliberately misleading ballot language designed to obscure its true effect (repealing abortion rights) represents a direct attack on the integrity of direct democracy and voter informed consent.

events.summary: Justice Elena Kagan, joined by Justices Ketanji Brown Jackson and Sonia Sotomayor, issued a dissent on May 22 to the Supreme Court's emergency order allowing Trump to remove independent agency heads without cause. events.title: FCC adopts rules prohibiting telecommunications certification bodies owned by foreign adversaries from equipment authorization program
events.summary: The Federal Communications Commission adopted a final rule establishing new requirements for telecommunications certification bodies (TCBs), test laboratories, and laboratory accreditation bodies participating in the equipment authorization program. events.title: Congressional Republicans pass One Big Beautiful Bill Act with temporary tax deductions expiring after Trump's presidency
events.summary: The Republican-controlled Congress passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act on Thursday with a narrow 215-214 vote. events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14301 on May 23, 2025, directing the Department of Energy to expedite the design, construction, and testing of advanced nuclear reactors. events.title: Trump issues Executive Order 14303 establishing "Gold Standard Science" framework for federal research and policy
events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14303 on May 23, 2025, establishing a "Gold Standard Science" framework requiring federal agencies to conduct research with reproducibility, transparency, and unbiased peer review. The order mandates agencies disclose data and models underlying influential scientific information, acknowledge uncertainties, avoid worst-case scenarios unless required by law, and revert to pre-2021 scientific integrity policies. Agency heads must report implementation within 60 days. The order explicitly criticizes prior COVID-19 school reopening guidance, whale population projections, and climate scenario modeling as examples of politicized science.
events.why_relevant: This order reshapes federal scientific governance by mandating rollback of 2021–2025 policies, restricting use of precautionary scenarios in agency decision-making, and establishing new enforcement mechanisms that could alter how agencies conduct environmental, public health, and climate assessments.
events.basis: By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America... it is hereby ordered: Section 1. Policy and Purpose... My Administration is committed to restoring a gold standard for science.

events.title: Trump signed Executive Order 14299 directing rapid deployment of advanced nuclear reactors at military installations and Department of Energy facilities to power AI infrastructure and critical defense systems.
events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14299 on May 23, 2025, establishing a national security policy to accelerate development and deployment of advanced nuclear reactor technologies. The order directs the Secretary of Defense to establish a program of record and commence operation of a nuclear reactor at a domestic military base by September 30, 2028. The Secretary of Energy must designate Department of Energy sites for advanced reactor deployment within 90 days, with operations targeted within 30 months. The order authorizes release of at least 20 metric tons of high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) from federal stockpiles, streamlines environmental review under NEPA through categorical exclusions, and directs aggressive pursuit of at least 20 new nuclear cooperation agreements with foreign partners to expand U.S. nuclear technology exports.
events.why_relevant: The order accelerates nuclear deployment at military and federal sites with expedited environmental review, expands access to weapons-usable nuclear materials, and prioritizes nuclear exports as a geopolitical tool, raising questions about oversight, nonproliferation safeguards, and democratic process in national security decisions.
events.basis: The Secretary of Defense, through the Secretary of the Army, shall commence the operation of a nuclear reactor, regulated by the United States Army, at a domestic military base or installation no later than September 30, 2028.

events.title: Trump signs Executive Order 14300 reforming Nuclear Regulatory Commission structure, regulations, and licensing timelines
events.summary: President Trump signed Executive Order 14300 on May 23, 2025, directing comprehensive reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to accelerate nuclear reactor licensing and deployment. The order mandates the NRC establish fixed 18-month deadlines for new reactor construction approvals and 1-year deadlines for operating license renewals, reorganize its structure with reductions in force, revise radiation safety standards away from the linear no-threshold model, streamline the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards, and complete wholesale regulatory revision within 18 months. The order reframes the NRC's mission to balance safety with promotion of nuclear energy as a national security priority.
events.why_relevant: The order fundamentally restructures an independent regulatory agency's statutory mission and operational constraints, subordinating safety-first regulatory culture to energy production acceleration and potentially weakening public health protections through revised radiation exposure standards.
events.basis: The NRC shall undertake reductions in force in conjunction with this reorganization" and "issue notice(s) of proposed rulemaking effecting this revision within 9 months" with deadlines of "no more than 18 months for final decision on an application to construct and operate a new reactor.

events.why_relevant: The order materially accelerates federal nuclear technology development by removing regulatory and procedural barriers, reshaping the Department of Energy's institutional capacity and timeline for advanced reactor deployment—a significant shift in energy policy and federal administrative process.
events.basis: Within 90 days of the date of this order, the Secretary shall take appropriate action to revise the regulations, guidance, and procedures and practices of the Department, the National Laboratories, and any other entity under the Department's jurisdiction to significantly expedite the review, approval, and deployment of advanced reactors.

events.title: Trump issues executive order reforming the Nuclear Regulatory Commission
events.summary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order on May 23, 2025, directing comprehensive reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). The order mandates restructuring the NRC's culture, personnel, and regulations to accelerate nuclear reactor licensing and deployment. Key directives include establishing fixed 18-month deadlines for new reactor approvals and 1-year deadlines for existing reactor licensing, reducing the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards, reconsidering radiation exposure models, and streamlining the public hearing process. The order aims to expand U.S. nuclear capacity from 100 GW to 400 GW by 2050.
events.why_relevant: The order materially weakens independent regulatory oversight of nuclear safety by subordinating the NRC's safety mandate to energy production goals and imposing strict timelines that may compromise thorough review, affecting democratic accountability and public health protection.
events.basis: Beginning today, my Administration will reform the NRC, including its structure, personnel, regulations, and basic operations.
